newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajikistan may legalise opposition parties.
newsitem.headline: Tajikistan may legalise opposition parties.

text.p: A senior Tajik official said on Tuesday the former Soviet republic, torn apart by four years of bitter civil war, was considering legalising opposition parties and organisations.
"We are going to look at the legalisation of opposition parties and political organisations at the talks," Talbak Nazarov, Tajikistan's foreign minister, told Reuters.
He spoke just before leaving for the Iranian capital Tehran where he will represent the government at a further round of peace negotiations with the country's armed Islamic opposition.
The main protagonists in the civil war agreed a ceasefire last December during talks in neighbouring Afghanistan which has largely held. A military deal was agreed last month in Moscow.
Nazarov will meet with opposition representative Akbar Torajonzoda in Tehran, with talks centering on a political settlement expected to last around 10 days.
"Organisations at the moment are mostly military-political," said Nazarov in reference to the remote, mountainous republic's kaleidescopic array of warlords and regional fiefdoms.
"They must disarm and become purely political organisations," Nazarov said.
However, some opposition leaders have expressed concern over the process of legalisation.
Dzhumaboy Niyazov, leader of the outlawed Democratic Party, told Reuters: "The government insists on disarming first before legalisation but we think it should be the other way round."
